```{python}
#| label: fig-bench-cube-vs-path
#| fig-cap: "Tree + CoordPath vs Tree + CoordCube: measured comparison for 9-path neighborhood (D=2, R=1, radius=1). Tree+Path (sequential): 9 CoordSpaceN2 lookups at 159 ns. Tree+Cube (dense store): proximity r=1 at 287 ns — cube adds BoundingBoxIter + Vec push overhead. Tree+Cube (sparse store, 9 entries): proximity r=1 at 48 ns — 3.3x faster than sequential. Cube advantages are spatial semantics (distance, region) and sparse-store throughput, not raw dense-store lookup speed."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

ops = [
    '9 sequential\nlookups\n(Tree+Path)',
    'Proximity r=1\n9 paths\n(Tree+Cube)',
    'Path gen only\n(empty tree)',
    '9 lookups\n(Dense+Path\nreference)',
]

times = [159.0, 287.0, 48.0, 15.4]
hatches = ['...', '...', '...', '///']
edges = ['black', 'black', 'black', 'black']

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5))
bars = ax.bar(range(len(ops)), times, color='white', edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.8, hatch=hatches)

ax.set_xticks(range(len(ops)))
ax.set_xticklabels(ops, fontsize=8)
ax.set_ylabel('ns (lower is better)')
ax.set_ylim(0, 230)

for bar, val in zip(bars, times):
    ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 5,
            f'{val} ns', ha='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold')

# Ratio annotations
ax.annotate('sequential
wins by 1.8x', xy=(1, 287), xytext=(1, 200),
            fontsize=8, ha='center', fontweight='bold',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.12', facecolor='white', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.9))

ax.annotate('cube wins
by 3.3x', xy=(2, 48), xytext=(2, 110),
            fontsize=9, ha='center', fontweight='bold', color='black',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.12', facecolor='white', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.9))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
